Back Pain in Jogeshwari — When Home Remedies Are Not Enough and a Doctor Is Needed

If your back pain lasts for more than a few weeks, keeps returning, interferes with daily activities, or becomes worse over time, it may indicate an underlying condition that requires medical attention. Common causes of chronic back pain include slipped discs, arthritis, spinal degeneration, nerve compression, and sports or workplace injuries. Early diagnosis can help prevent complications and improve recovery outcomes.

ECG Test in Jogeshwari — What It Detects and Why Doctors Recommend It

An Electrocardiogram (ECG) is one of the most commonly recommended heart tests and plays an important role in evaluating heart health. The test records the electrical activity of the heart and helps doctors identify potential cardiac problems quickly and non-invasively.

Doctors may recommend an ECG if a patient experiences symptoms such as chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, dizziness, or unexplained fatigue. The test can help detect irregular heart rhythms (arrhythmias), signs of a previous heart attack, reduced blood flow to the heart, and other abnormalities that may affect heart function.

An ECG is also commonly used as part of routine health screenings for individuals with high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or a family history of heart disease. Early detection of heart-related issues allows for timely treatment and better long-term outcomes.

If you are experiencing heart-related symptoms or have risk factors for cardiovascular disease, consulting a cardiologist in Jogeshwari can help determine whether an ECG is required. Consulting a cardiologist in Jogeshwari can help detect potential heart problems before they become serious.

A heart checkup is also recommended for people experiencing chest discomfort, shortness of breath, dizziness, heart palpitations, or unexplained fatigue. Routine tests such as blood pressure monitoring, ECG, cholesterol screening, and other cardiac assessments can provide valuable insights into your heart health. Early diagnosis allows for timely treatment and lifestyle modifications that may help prevent future complications.

featured_reviews.name: Parag
featured_reviews.review_text:
Update: I’ve experienced both private consultation and general OPD at Holy Spirit Hospital, and overall, it has been a bad experience.

The campus itself is beautiful and well maintained. Online appointment booking is smooth, while offline booking starts at 7:30 am and doctors typically begin consultations from around 8:30 am.

The private consultation experience (ENT, in my case) was genuinely good. The doctor gave adequate time, listened patiently, and the interaction felt reassuring and professional. However, this comes at a cost, as the visit including diagnostics ended up in the range of ₹3,000–4,000.

The general OPD experience was very bad. The charges are in the range of ₹400-700.

Earlier I had positive experiences with  Gastroenterology and Surgery. I was very much impressed with the surgeon, but his opinion was outrightly dismissed by 3 other senior surgeons and physicians. I realised he kept focussing on a know problem which wasn't connected to my pain.  Gastroenterologist doesn't do any physical examination to understand the location of pain or confirm hemorrhoids. Seems, he only checks you during pricey colonoscopy and endoscopy procedures.

My experience with General Medicine and Urology OPD was disappointing. In these departments, the main doctor and an assistant doctor sit at the same small table and consult two different patients simultaneously.

In General Medicine OPD, there were up to four patients along with their attendants inside the same room at once—one with the main doctor, one with the assistant, one waiting behind the doctor, and another at the entrance being triaged for blood pressure and weight. That easily translates to 8–10 people in a single consultation room. There is no space for discussion, questions, nuance, or privacy. The doctor barely had time for eye contact, let alone a detailed conversation or examination.

In the Urology OPD, I could speak to the actual doctor only after the assistant doctor felt I was not convinced. While I do not question the competence of junior doctors, as a patient it feels unfair when you do not get adequate time with the consultant you booked.

I guess this is the truth of INR 400-700 consultations. I sincerely hope the PRO and hospital administration take note of these inconsistencies, especially given Holy Spirit’s reputation as an esteemed institution.

Dear Parag,

We have carefully read your review and the multiple updates you have made over time. While we respect your right to share experiences, repeated edits with selective interpretations create confusion rather than clarity for the public.

Holy Spirit Hospital has been serving the community for over 57 years with a clear mission:
➡️ to provide ethical, quality medical care at affordable costs, especially for patients who are financially constrained.

It is important to place a few facts on record for transparency:

1️⃣ General OPD vs Private Consultation

Holy Spirit Hospital deliberately maintains low-cost General OPD consultations (₹400–₹700) so that patients from all economic backgrounds can access senior medical care. This is a conscious, charitable decision — not a compromise in quality.

Some consultants also run private OPD sessions at charges decided by them, purely for convenience and extended consultation time.
➡️ The hospital does not interfere in private OPD fees.

Comparing a low-cost charitable OPD with a private consultation model is not an apples-to-apples comparison.

2️⃣ Consultation Cost with Diagnostics

Your claim of ₹3,000–₹4,000 includes diagnostic investigations.
Any investigation—whether blood tests, imaging, or endoscopy—is:

Done only if clinically required

Clearly chargeable, as per standard medical practice anywhere in the world

This is not unique to Holy Spirit Hospital.

3️⃣ Regarding Junior Doctors

The doctors you refer to as “assistants” are not casual or unqualified staff.
They are:

Postgraduate doctors (MD/MS/DNB)

Having completed 3 years of rigorous specialty training

Working under direct supervision of senior consultants with 25–35+ years of experience

They are competent, qualified, and trained to evaluate patients thoroughly.
If a patient requests direct interaction with the senior consultant, that is always accommodated.

4️⃣ Multiple Patients in OPD Rooms

General OPD caters to high patient volumes, precisely because of its affordability. This allows thousands of patients daily—many of whom cannot afford private healthcare—to receive treatment from experienced specialists.

This model is transparent, intentional, and patient-centric, not neglectful.

5️⃣ Allegation of Doctors “Pushing Procedures”

Any invasive procedure such as endoscopy or colonoscopy is recommended only after clinical assessment, based on medical guidelines—not for revenue generation. Suggesting otherwise without evidence is a serious misrepresentation of ethical medical practice.

6️⃣ Repeated Updates to the Same Review

Repeatedly modifying the same review with escalating commentary, despite explanations, raises concerns about intent.
Constructive feedback is always welcome; repeated public reinterpretation without engagement does not help patients or institutions improve.

You have shared your Hospital ID, and we reiterate our request:
➡️ Please meet our PRO or Medical Administration so this can be discussed clinically and factually, rather than through ongoing public speculation.

Holy Spirit Hospital remains committed to:

Ethical medicine

Training future specialists

Serving patients who otherwise would have no access to quality healthcare

We stand by our doctors, our systems, and our mission.
